1.2.3.12-r2.burton_quote: amongst other herbs, he should cut up the Weed of Covetousness by the roots, that there be no remainder left, and then know this for a certainty

1.2.3.12-r3.burton_quote: With what art thou not weary? With getting money. What is most delectable? To gain.

1.2.3.12-r5.burton_quote: troubled in his abundance, and sorrowful in plenty, unhappy for the present, and more unhappy in the life to come

1.2.3.12-r6.burton_quote: compares it to Hell; which devours all, and yet never hath enough
1.2.3.12-r6.translation: it has no limit; the more it has, the needier it is.

1.2.3.12-r7.burton_quote: he was loath to fling away the foul water, complaining that he was undone, because the smoke got out of his roof
